intro_html: Three main ingredients, one slow cooker, and dinner is basically done. Sugar-free maple syrup and dijon mustard glaze lean pork tenderloin until it is tender and just a little sweet, served over potatoes with green beans. It runs around $3.71 a serving (at everyday cost) and gives you 59 grams of protein across 14 bowls.
cost_closing_html: About $3.71 a bowl (at everyday cost) for a high-protein dinner that beats takeout on price and macros.
portion_html: Each of the 14 servings comes in at 59 grams of protein and just 565 calories.
upsell_html: When a meal is this easy and this cheap, there is no reason not to keep it in the rotation. Members get every recipe in the Meal Prep section, plus the full library of money lessons and tools, all for $1 a month.
shop_smart: Sugar-free maple syrup keeps this glaze sweet without the sugar hit. Buy one bottle of sugar-free syrup and it lasts through many batches.
Frozen green beans cost less than fresh and never spoil on you. Keep bags of frozen green beans on hand for meals like this.
A ten pound bag of potatoes is the cheapest way to buy them. Buy the big potato bag and you will use every last one.
make_it: Place the pork tenderloin in the slow cooker.
Stir the sugar-free maple syrup, dijon mustard, and garlic powder together, then pour it over the pork.
Cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours until the pork is fork tender.
Steam the green beans just until crisp-tender near the end.
Roast or boil the potatoes until soft.
Slice or shred the pork, serve it over potatoes, and add the green beans on the side.
